verdict.overall: Since Sunday, the biggest shifts are NVDA and ZETA flipping toward supportive setups even as their prices slipped, while PLTR's range dropped sharply lower with earnings landing today - the sharpest change on the board. TSLA stays stuck in an opposing setup despite its uptrend, and AMAT's range narrowed with earnings approaching; confidence is rising for NVDA and ZETA's floors holding, but falling for PLTR and AMAT given earnings risk and broadly pricey options across the board.

tickers.TSLA: Since Sunday: little changed - still opposing across all four expiries despite a 1% price rise. The near-term floor rose to 380 and ceiling pulled in to 410, but the structure still caps TSLA below its magnet levels, and options remain pricey.
tickers.PLTR: Since Sunday: weaker - price fell 3%, and the nearest magnet dropped to 187.5 with floor sliding to 155 and ceiling to 195, a lower, wider range. Earnings land today (11-02), adding real event risk on top of already very pricey options.
tickers.NVDA: Since Sunday: stronger - the nearest expiry flipped from neutral to supportive even as price dipped 1.3%, with the 200 floor holding firm. Earnings arrive 11-17, inside this window, likely bringing a volatility jump that could reshape the range.
tickers.ZETA: Since Sunday: stronger - three of four expiries flipped to supportive and the 30 floor has held despite a 2% price drop. Earnings hit 11-09, and options are already very pricey, so moves could be sharp heading into that date.
tickers.AMAT: Since Sunday: weaker - price dropped 4% and the 11-20 ceiling was pulled in sharply from 440 to 400, showing less confidence further out. All four weeks stay neutral. Earnings land 11-12, adding uncertainty on top of already pricey options.
tickers.AVGO: Since Sunday: little changed - price eased 1.2% and the nearest magnet and floor nudged down slightly (345 and 292.5), but all four expiries remain neutral. Earnings aren't until December, so no event risk sits inside this window.
tickers.GOOGL: No Sunday baseline. GOOGL is oversold (RSI near 21) in a downtrend but has the cheapest options on this list, sitting neutral through all four expiries with magnets drifting up from 285 to 315. Unusually busy trading today near the near-term magnet means it may be less reliable this week.
tickers.APP: Since Sunday: little changed - price barely moved but magnet levels drifted lower across all four expiries, staying neutral. Earnings land 11-04, just two days away, and options are already very pricey, so expect a big reaction.
tickers.BE: No Sunday baseline. BE stays neutral through all four expiries in a downtrend, with the floor holding between 170 and 190 and fairly priced options. No earnings fall inside this four-week window.
tickers.SPY: Since Sunday: little changed - price eased 0.5% and the nearest magnet slipped to 764 (£109.53) with the ceiling pulling in to 770 (£110.39), but all four expiries stay neutral. Options remain pricey, which is typical for this index fund.
tickers.QQQ: Since Sunday: little changed - price fell 1.4% with magnets drifting down slightly (714, roughly £80.48 nearest) but all four expiries hold neutral. Options are pricey. GBP figures for ISUS are rough since it only partly tracks the Nasdaq.
